findings.title: SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym can raise NoMethodError
findings.body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` calls `to_sym` on the setting value before any nil check. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` is nil or blank (e.g. during early boot, before site settings are provisioned, or in a DB-less/migration context), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'to_sym' for nil`. Since this method is invoked on every I18n fallback lookup and from `ensure_loaded!` in a before_filter, a single nil setting breaks all translation. The trailing `.compact` cannot help because the exception happens while building the array; guard with `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` instead.

findings.title: Translation LRU cache key ignores fallback locales
findings.body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With the new Fallbacks backend, the resolved value for a given key/locale also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (the second entry of FallbackLocaleList). After an admin changes the site default locale, previously cached entries resolved through the old fallback remain in the LRU cache and are served, producing stale/incorrect translations until a process restart or `I18n.reload!`. The fallback chain (or default_locale) should be part of the cache key, or the cache must be invalidated when default_locale changes.

findings.title: Fallback locales only loaded in web requests; jobs/mailers get missing translations
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Because `translate` lazily loads only `config.locale`, any code path outside a controller request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console, console-driven digests) performing a lookup in a locale with a missing key will have the fallback locale's YAML not loaded, so the Fallbacks backend finds nothing and raises/returns a missing-translation instead of the fallback string. The loading should be hooked into the lookup path (e.g. inside `translate`/`load_locale`) or into the job/mailer locale setup as well.

findings.title: translate can NoMethodError on nil @loaded_locales
findings.body: `translate` does `@loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)` without initializing `@loaded_locales`, while the newly added `ensure_loaded!` defensively does `@loaded_locales ||= []`. If any translation happens before `reload!` has run (the only place that initializes the ivar), `translate` raises `NoMethodError` on nil. Initialize the ivar consistently (e.g. `@loaded_locales ||= []` in `translate` too) rather than relying on call ordering.

findings.title: ensure_loaded!/@loaded_locales initialization is not thread-safe
findings.body: `I18n.ensure_loaded!` reads and lazily initializes `@loaded_locales` outside `LOAD_MUTEX` (only `load_locale` takes the lock). Under concurrent requests on a threaded server, two threads can simultaneously see nil/stale arrays and `@loaded_locales << locale` from different threads can lose entries, causing redundant loads or a locale being considered loaded while its translations are only partially installed. Perform the check and initialization under the same mutex.

findings.title: No tests for fallback behaviour
findings.body: This PR introduces a new fallback chain (user locale -> site default locale -> :en) plus lazy loading of fallback locale files, but adds no specs. There is no coverage asserting that a key missing in the user locale resolves from the site default locale and then from English, nor that fallback locale YAML is actually loaded before lookup. Given the silent-failure mode (missing translation strings shown to users), a spec for FallbackLocaleList#[] and an end-to-end translation fallback spec should be added.
